items.title: Public Preview: On-prem NAS share discovery and assessment are now available using Azure Migrate
items.description:
Azure Migrate now supports discovery and assessment for network-attached storage, allowing customers and partners to plan migrations of Dell PowerScale (OneFS) and NetApp ONTAP storage to Azure. The Azure Migrate appliance connects directly to your NAS clusters using read-only credentials, inventories every SMB, NFS, and S3 share, and evaluates each share against Azure Files, Azure Blob Storage, and Azure NetApp Files. 

Key benefits include: 

  • Discover Dell PowerScale/Isilon and NetApp ONTAP/FAS clusters and the shares they host 
  • Group, tag, and filter NAS shares alongside your existing server, application, and database inventory 
  • Assess each share with readiness, a right-sized Azure target configuration, and monthly cost estimates 
  • Generate a business case comparing Azure storage services against on-premises cost, and sequence moves using wave plans 

This capability replaces manual, spreadsheet-driven NAS planning with a verified per-share inventory and a defensible cost basis, especially for large or multi-protocol storage estates. 

NAS is often the largest and least-understood part of an on-premises estate. Bringing NAS discovery and assessment into Azure Migrate means storage is planned in the same project, and the same business case, as the servers and applications that depend on it. 

Getting started: 

To get started, update your Azure Migrate appliance, add your NAS cluster as a discovery source, and run an assessment directly from the Azure portal. Write to us at azurestoragemigrations@microsoft.com with questions or feedback. 

Learn more.

items.title: Retirement: OT security in Microsoft Defender for IoT
items.description:
This is the formal notice that Microsoft plans to deprecate the operational technology (OT) security component of Microsoft Defender for IoT. The service will be fully deprecated in October 2029, following a three-year transition period.

This change applies only to Defender for IoT OT Security. Enterprise IoT capabilities in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint are not affected. Device discovery and vulnerability assessment will continue to be available.

When this will happen

Deprecation is planned for October 2029. This notice begins the transition period and does not require you to immediately stop using your existing deployment. Complete your migration to an alternative OT security solution before retirement.

How this will affect your organization

If you use Defender for IoT OT Security, you will need to transition to an alternative solution before October 2029. During the transition, the service will remain supported with routine security updates and bug fixes, but no new OT-specific capabilities or feature investments will be introduced. Existing customer agreements and renewals will be honored through October 2029.

What you can do to prepare

  1. Assess your environment. Review existing OT deployments, sensors, integrations, licenses, contracts, and security requirements.

  2. Evaluate your options. Select an OT security solution that meets your organization’s needs. Microsoft offers connectors for Armis, Dragos, and Forescout, but you are not required to use a specific provider. OT data connectors in Microsoft Security Exposure Management support these three providers.

  3. Understand Microsoft integrations. Supported third-party OT connectors can bring OT asset and vulnerability data into Microsoft Security Exposure Management and the Defender portal. Third-party solutions require separate licensing and deployment.

  4. Build your transition plan. Account for procurement, testing, operational validation, continuity, data export, and sensor decommissioning, with migration completed before October 2029.

  5. Engage early. Contact OT security providers directly or work with your Microsoft account team to help coordinate an introduction.

Learn more:

  • OT data connectors 
  • Data connectors overview 
  • Enterprise IoT

items.title: Generally Available: Change from virtual network integration to a private endpoint capable network configuration in Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server
items.description:
You now have greater flexibility in network design for Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server workloads. Now you can change existing VNet-integrated servers from delegated-subnet networking to a private endpoint-capable configuration, enabling secure access over a private IP address through Azure Private Link. The migration retains existing backups; however, you should plan for a temporary connectivity interruption and configure a private endpoint or appropriate firewall rules after migration. 

Learn more.

items.title: Retirement: Azure Fluid Relay
items.description:
On February 2, 2027, we will retire Azure Fluid Relay. After this date, Azure Fluid Relay will reach end of availability, and workloads that continue to depend on the service may experience disruption.

The Fluid Framework remains available as an open-source framework for building distributed, real-time collaborative web applications. A self-hosted Fluid service solution is available as the replacement. You can continue using Azure Fluid Relay until February 1, 2027 while you complete your transition.

How this affects you:
If your applications continue to use Azure Fluid Relay after February 2, 2027, they may experience service disruption. Moving to the self-hosted solution means that you will be responsible for hosting and operating the Fluid service in your environment. Operational and infrastructure costs will depend on your deployment architecture, scale, and operational requirements.

What you need to do:
Transition workloads that depend on Azure Fluid Relay to a self-hosted Fluid service solution before February 2, 2027. Review your Azure subscriptions and identify applications that use Azure Fluid Relay, plan and complete the transition, and use the self-hosted Fluid service solution in the Fluid Framework GitHub repository as the migration and replacement resource.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Storage Actions adds automatic task updates, execution controls, and case-sensitive matching
items.description:
Azure Storage Actions is introducing three enhancements to simplify task management and give you more control over automated data operations across Azure Blob and Data Lake Storage:
  • Automatic propagation of task definition updates: When you update a storage task definition the changes now automatically apply to its existing assignments. Scheduled assignment runs use the updated definition on their next run, keeping your data management logic consistent without updating each assignment individually.
  • Stop in-progress task assignment runs: You can request a stop for an individual task assignment’s in-progress run or across all assignments associated with a storage task. This gives you greater control when a run needs to be interrupted. Stop requests are processed asynchronously.
  • Case-sensitive operators: Target data more precisely with case-sensitive variants of `equals`, `contains`, `startsWith`, `endsWith`, and `matches` string operators. These additional operators provide you more flexibility, helping you select the intended blobs when capitalization matters. Existing operators retain their case-insensitive behavior.
Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Restart databases in Azure SQL DB via the Azure portal
items.description:
You can now restart or fail over databases directly from the Azure portal, including single databases, Hyperscale databases, and databases in elastic pools, without writing scripts against the Rest API or contacting support. 

 Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Geo-Replication on partitioned namespaces for Azure Service Bus Premium
items.description:
Geo-Replication on partitioned namespaces for Azure Service Bus Premium is now generally available. You can now combine the throughput benefits of partitioning with the reliability of replicating your messages and metadata to a secondary Azure region. 

Partitioned namespaces distribute queues and topics across multiple message brokers and messaging stores within a region, allowing throughput to scale beyond a single broker. 

You can enable Geo-Replication on an existing partitioned Premium namespace or configure both capabilities on a new namespace. 

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Azure Site Recovery for Azure Local
items.description:
Azure Site Recovery support for Azure Local is now generally available, making enterprise-grade disaster recovery simpler, accessible, easier to setup and secure than ever before. Customers can protect supported Windows and Linux virtual machines by replicating workloads to Azure, extending their disaster recovery capabilities to the cloud.

With streamlined setup in the Azure portal, customers can validate their recovery plans without disrupting production replication, fail over to Azure during planned or unplanned outages, and return workloads to Azure Local when their on-premises environment is ready. The capability is available in all Azure Local-supported regions.

Learn more: 

  • Tech Community blog 
  • Official documentation
